# Peregrine Falcon Migration (1973-75)

## Bill Cochran Study

This study tracked peregrine falcon migration patterns using early radio telemetry technology, revolutionizing our understanding of raptor movement and navigation.

This research provided the first detailed documentation of individual falcon migration routes, flight speeds, and stopover behaviours across North America.

![](images/clipboard-4078089510.png)

### Setting up Libraries:

```{r}
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)

# Run this in your console first
# devtools::install_github("ropensci/rnaturalearthhires")
library(rnaturalearthhires)

# Plotting Maps
library(tidyverse) # Maps using ggplot() + geom_sf()
library(ggformula) # Maps using gf_sf()
library(tmap) # Thematic Maps, static and interactive
library(tmaptools)
library(tmap.mapgl)
library(osmdata) # Fetch map data from osmdata.org
library(sfheaders) # Handcrafted Map data
## Interactive Maps
library(leaflet) # interactive Maps
library(leaflet)
library(leaflet.providers)
library(leaflet.extras)
library(threejs) # Globe maps in R. Part of the htmlwidgets family of packages

# For Spatial Data Frame Processing
library(sf)
library(lubridate)
```

### Reading the Data:

```{r}
lines <- st_read("D:/files from desktop/R/Ihinas-experiments-with-R/posts/bird data/lines.shp")
points <- st_read("D:/files from desktop/R/Ihinas-experiments-with-R/posts/bird data/points.shp")
```

### Mapping it out:

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = lines, color = "black", 
          linewidth = 0.025) +   
  geom_sf(data = points, color = '#ff9999', linewidth = 0.5) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust =2 )
  ) +
  coord_sf() +
  labs(title = "Peregrine Falcon Migration (1973–75)",
       subtitle = "Bill Cochran Study | Source: Movebank") +
  theme_minimal()

```

### Let us look at the different Peregrine Falcons:

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = points,aes(color = tag_ident)) +
  geom_sf(data=lines, color = "black", linewidth= 0.02)+
 theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust =2 )
  ) +
  coord_sf() +
  labs(title = "Peregrine Falcon Migration (1973–75)",
       subtitle = "Bill Cochran Study | Source: Movebank") +
  theme_minimal()
```

All three falcons follow a general north-to-south migration pattern through central North America.

The clustering of points suggests that there are multiple stopover sites where falcons remained stationary for extended periods.

-   Peregrine #5 shows the longest and most extensive migration, traveling the farthest south.

-   Peregrine #1 has a much shorter route, primarily clustered in the northern portion around Peregrine #4 shows a pattern with looping, this suggests that the bird was flying within a relatively small area rather than continuing its migration.

This could mean:

-   Favourable hunting grounds

-   Energy conservation

-   It was waiting for favorable migration conditions

### Plotting this on the world map:

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = World, fill = "grey90", color = "grey") +
  geom_sf(data = points,aes(color = tag_ident)) +
  geom_sf(data=lines, color = "black", linewidth= 0.01)+
 theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust =2 )
  ) +
  coord_sf() +
  labs(title = "Peregrine Falcon Migration (1973–75)",
       subtitle = "Bill Cochran Study | Source: Movebank") +
  theme_minimal()

```

This shows us that all migration occurs within the central USA.

### Plotting it on the USA map:

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = World %>% filter(name=="United States of America"),
          fill = "grey90", color = "grey") +
  geom_sf(data = points,aes(color = tag_ident)) +
  geom_sf(data=lines, color = "black", linewidth= 0.01)+
 theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust =2 )
  ) +
  coord_sf() +
  labs(title = "Peregrine Falcon Migration (1973–75)",
       subtitle = "Bill Cochran Study | Source: Movebank") +
  theme_minimal()

```

The migration corridor appears to avoid both coasts, staying inland.

### How did migration change through the years 1973 - 1975:

Only plotted points(resting locations) and not lines (movement) as there is no timestamp for it.

#### Mutating data:

```{r}
points_mod1 <- points %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(ymd_hms(timestamp)),
    year_category = case_when(
      year == 1973 ~ "Year_73",
      year == 1974 ~ "Year_74",
      year == 1975 ~ "Year_75",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )
```

#### Migration in 1973:

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = World %>% filter(name=="United States of America"),
          fill = "grey90", color = "grey") +
  geom_sf(data = points_mod1 %>% filter(year==1973),
          aes(color = tag_ident)) +
 theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust =2 )
  ) +
  coord_sf() +
  labs(title = "Peregrine Falcon Migration in 1973",
       subtitle = "Bill Cochran Study | Source: Movebank") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Only Peregrine#1 rested, concentrated in a small area in the central USA.

#### Migration in 1974:

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = World %>% filter(name=="United States of America"),
          fill = "grey90", color = "grey") +
  geom_sf(data = points_mod1 %>% filter(year==1974),
          aes(color = tag_ident)) +
 theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust =2 )
  ) +
  coord_sf() +
  labs(title = "Peregrine Falcon Migration in 1974",
       subtitle = "Bill Cochran Study | Source: Movebank") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Assumption: No falcons rested?? Or no falcons tracked?

#### Migration in 1975:

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = World %>% filter(name=="United States of America"),
          fill = "grey90", color = "grey") +
  geom_sf(data = points_mod1 %>% filter(year==1975),
          aes(color = tag_ident)) +
 theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust =2 )
  ) +
  coord_sf() +
  labs(title = "Peregrine Falcon Migration in 1975",
       subtitle = "Bill Cochran Study | Source: Movebank") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Both Peregrine#4 andPeregrine#5 show multiple rest stops along the migration corridor, this suggests that falcons migrate in stages rather than continuously.

**Assumption:** Peregrine#1 has completed its migration in 1973 itself.
